messages.content:
Let \( a_0, a_1, a_2, \ldots \) be the unique sequence of nonnegative integers less than 397 with \( a_0 = 1 \) and

\[ a_{n+1}(a_n + 1)^2 \equiv a_n \pmod{397} \]

for all nonnegative integers \( n \). Given that \( a_{2026} = 9 \), compute the remainder when \( a_0 + a_1 + \cdots + a_{2026} \) is divided by 397.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
All congruences are modulo \(397\). Since \(397\) is prime and the sequence exists, no term can be \(0\) or \(396\), so every \(a_n\) is invertible.

Let

\[
b_n \equiv a_n^{-1} \pmod{397}.
\]

From

\[
a_{n+1}(a_n+1)^2 \equiv a_n,
\]

we get

\[
a_{n+1}^{-1} \equiv a_n^{-1}(a_n+1)^2.
\]

Thus

\[
b_{n+1} \equiv a_n + 2 + a_n^{-1}
= b_n + a_n + 2.
\]

Rearranging,

\[
a_n \equiv b_{n+1}-b_n-2.
\]

Summing from \(n=0\) to \(2026\),

\[
a_0+a_1+\cdots+a_{2026}
\equiv b_{2027}-b_0-2\cdot 2027.
\]

Now \(b_0=a_0^{-1}=1\). Also \(a_{2026}=9\), so

\[
b_{2026}\equiv 9^{-1}\pmod{397}.
\]

Since \(9\cdot 44=396\equiv -1\), we have \(9^{-1}\equiv -44\equiv 353\). Therefore

\[
b_{2027}\equiv b_{2026}+a_{2026}+2
\equiv 353+9+2
\equiv 364.
\]

So

\[
a_0+\cdots+a_{2026}
\equiv 364-1-4054.
\]

Since \(4054\equiv 84\pmod{397}\),

\[
364-1-84=279.
\]

\[
\boxed{279}
\]
